package: HTSSOP-20 (TI PWP0020T, PowerPAD TSSOP, 6.5 mm x 4.4 mm, 0.65 mm pitch)
description: TI TPS16630, 4.5 V to 60 V / 0.6 A to 6 A eFuse (smart high-side switch) with 31 mohm integrated FET, adjustable current limit (ILIM), adjustable UVLO and adjustable overvoltage CUTOFF (OVP), adjustable output slew-rate / inrush control (dVdT), analog current monitor (IMON), open-drain FLT and PGOOD, and MODE-selectable latch-off vs auto-retry. Datasheet: TPS1663x, SLVSET9G, Rev G, April 2026 (48 pages) - the TPS16630 is the OVP-cutoff variant with no PLIM pin. DESIGN BLOCKER FOR DEFAULT-OFF RAILS: the enable control is an ACTIVE-LOW shutdown pin named SHDN, not an active-high enable. SHDN is internally pulled up - the open-circuit pin voltage is 2.48 V min / 2.7 V typ / 3.3 V max (sec 6.5) against a 2 V rising enable threshold, so a FLOATING SHDN LEAVES THE DEVICE ON. Holding the output off with the MCU absent, in reset, or tri-stated REQUIRES an external pull-down on SHDN that sinks at least 10 uA while keeping the pin below the 0.8 V V(SHUTF) threshold (sec 8.3.11). Programming for this design: R(ILIM) = 18 / I(OL) [kohm, A] (Eq 6/10) -> 18 kohm for a 1.0 A limit, which is exactly TI's own 1 A worked example in sec 9.2. MODE left OPEN gives latch-off; MODE shorted to GND gives auto-retry.

pinout.name: IN
pinout.notes: Power input; connects to the DRAIN of the internal FET. IN is pins 1, 2 and 3 on HTSSOP - all three must be connected (sec 8.3.9: 'Do not leave any of the IN and OUT pins un-connected').

pinout.name: IN
pinout.notes: Power input, parallel with pins 1 and 3. Must be connected.

pinout.name: IN
pinout.notes: Power input, parallel with pins 1 and 2. Must be connected.

pinout.name: N.C
pinout.notes: No connect (Table 5-1).

pinout.name: N.C
pinout.notes: No connect (Table 5-1).

pinout.name: P_IN
pinout.notes: Supply voltage of the device. Table 5-1: 'Always connect P_IN to IN directly.' Sec 8.3.9 repeats: 'Connect P_IN and IN together.'

pinout.name: UVLO
pinout.notes: Programmable undervoltage lockout input (Table 5-1 TYPE = I). Falling below V(UVLOF) turns the internal FET off quickly and asserts FLT. V(UVLOR) = 1.176 / 1.2 / 1.224 V rising, V(UVLOF) = 1.09 / 1.122 / 1.15 V falling, hysteresis 78 mV typ, threshold accuracy +/-2%. Set with the R1(IN-UVLO) / R2(UVLO-OVP) / R3(OVP-GND) divider of Figure 8-3: V(UVLOR) = (R2+R3)/(R1+R2+R3) x V(UV)  [Eq 12]. Sec 8.3.2: 'UVLO terminal must not be left floating'; tie UVLO to IN if the function is not used. Pin leakage I(UVLO) = +/-150 nA max, so pick divider current I(R123) >= 20x the UVLO/OVP pin leakage (sec 9.2.2.2). Rated to 60 V rec / 67 V abs max. Toggling UVLO low->high also resets a latched-off fault (Table 8-1).

pinout.name: OVP
pinout.notes: Adjustable overvoltage CUTOFF input, TPS16630 only (Table 5-1 TYPE = I). Exceeding V(OVPR) turns the internal FET off and asserts FLT. V(OVPR) = 1.176 / 1.2 / 1.224 V rising, V(OVPF) = 1.09 / 1.122 / 1.15 V falling, +/-2% accuracy. Set with the same divider: V(OVPR) = R3/(R1+R2+R3) x V(OV)  [Eq 11]. Turn-off delay OVP_toff(dly) = 11 us typ; re-enable delay OVP_ton(dly) = 150 + 49.5 x C(dVdT)[nF] us. Pin leakage +/-150 nA max. CAUTION: unlike UVLO, OVP is a LOW-VOLTAGE pin - rec op 0-4 V, abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V; it must never see the raw input rail.

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Connect GND to system ground (Table 5-1).

pinout.name: dVdT
pinout.notes: Output slew-rate / inrush control (Table 5-1 TYPE = I/O). A capacitor from dVdT to GND sets the OUT slew rate at power-up. t(dVdT) = 20.8e3 x V(IN) x C(dVdT) [Eq 2, V in volts, C in farads, t in seconds]; I(INRUSH) = C(OUT) x V(IN) / t(dVdT) [Eq 1]. Internals: I(dVdT) = 2 uA typ charging, GAIN(dVdT) = 25 V/V (V(OUT)/V(dVdT)), V(dVdTmax) = 4.17 V typ, R(dVdT) discharge = 16.6 ohm typ. LEAVING dVdT FLOATING gives the fastest ramp (24 V / 500 us) and enables power-up in thermal regulation so the part charges large and unknown capacitive loads by regulating TJ at T(J_REG) = 145 C typ; if OUT has not powered up within t(Treg_timeout) = 1.25 s typ the FET turns OFF and the MODE setting decides latch-off vs auto-retry (sec 8.3.1.1). Recommended C(dVdT) minimum is 10 nF when used; timing specs are given for C(dVdT) >= 10 nF. Rec op 0-4 V, abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V, sink current 10 mA abs max.

pinout.name: ILIM
pinout.notes: Overload current-limit programming (Table 5-1 TYPE = I/O). Resistor from ILIM to GND. R(ILIM) = 18 / I(OL), R in kohm and I(OL) in A [Eq 6 and Eq 10]. FOR A 1.0 A LIMIT: R(ILIM) = 18 kohm, 1% - this is TI's own worked example (Table 9-1 design requirement I(LIM) = 1 A, sec 9.2.2.1 'Select the closest standard 1% resistor value: R(ILIM) = 18 kohm', and Figures 8-6/8-7/8-8 are captured at R(ILIM) = 18 kohm). Recommended R(ILIM) range 3 kohm to 30 kohm; UL 2367 recognition (File E169910) requires R(ILIM) >= 3 kohm. Measured accuracy points: 30 kohm -> 0.54/0.6/0.66 A, 9 kohm -> 1.84/2.0/2.16 A, 4.02 kohm -> 4.185/4.5/4.815 A, 3 kohm -> 5.58/6.0/6.42 A (features claim +/-7%). Fast-trip threshold I(FASTTRIP) = 2 x I(OL); hard short-circuit threshold I(SCP) = 45 A with 1 us typ response. ILIM open or shorted to GND is detected and holds the FET OFF until cleared (sec 8.3.4.1). Rec op 0-4 V (implied), abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V, source current internally limited.

pinout.name: MODE
pinout.notes: Overload / power-limit / thermal fault response select (Table 5-1 TYPE = I; Table 8-1). MODE = OPEN (unconnected): active current limiting for a maximum of t(CL_PLIM)(dly) = 162 ms typ, THEN LATCHES OFF; the latch is reset by toggling SHDN or UVLO low->high, or by power-cycling IN. MODE = SHORTED TO GND: active current limiting for the same 162 ms then AUTO-RETRIES after t(TSD_retry) = 648 ms typ. For a latch-off design, leave MODE unconnected (do not stuff a resistor). Rec op 0-4 V, abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V, source current internally limited.

pinout.name: SHDN
pinout.notes: ACTIVE-LOW low-Iq shutdown - this is the only enable control; there is no active-high EN pin. DEFAULT STATE WITH NO EXTERNAL DRIVE IS ON: sec 6.5 specifies V(SHDN) open-circuit voltage = 2.48 V min / 2.7 V typ / 3.3 V max at I(SHDN) = 0.1 uA (an internal pull-up, shown as the 2.7 V source in the Figure 8-2 block diagram), and the enable threshold V(SHUTR) is 2 V rising - so a floating SHDN sits above the enable threshold and the FET turns ON. Shutdown threshold V(SHUTF) = 0.8 V falling; entry delay tSD(dly) = 1 us typ; Iq drops to 21 uA typ (60 uA max) in shutdown. Sec 8.3.11: 'To assert SHDN low, the pull down must have sinking capability of at least 10 uA. To enable the device, SHDN must be pulled up to at least 2 V.' I(SHDN) leakage at V(SHDN) = 0 V is -10 uA max. AN EXTERNAL PULL-DOWN TO GND IS THEREFORE MANDATORY for a default-off rail, and the MCU GPIO must drive SHDN high (>= 2 V) against it to enable. Cycling SHDN low->high also resets a latched-off fault. Rec op 0-5 V, abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V - SHDN is NOT rail-tolerant, never expose it to the 48 V input.

pinout.name: IMON
pinout.notes: Analog current-monitor output (Table 5-1 TYPE = O): sources a scaled copy of the FET current; a resistor from IMON to GND converts it to a voltage. V(IMON) = I(OUT) x GAIN(IMON) x R(IMON) [Eq 9], GAIN(IMON) = 27.9 uA/A typ (+/-6%): 25.66-30.14 uA/A for 0.6 A <= I(OUT) < 2 A and 26.22-29.58 uA/A for 2 A <= I(OUT) <= 6 A. Maximum usable V(IMON) is 4 V, which caps R(IMON); recommended R(IMON) minimum is 1 kohm and TI's 1 A example uses R(IMON) = 30 kohm (0.84 V at 1.0 A). Sec 8.3.6: 'The IMON pin must not have a bypass capacitor to avoid delay in the current monitoring information.' Leave floating if unused. Rec op 0-4 V, abs max -0.3 to 5.5 V.

pinout.name: FLT
pinout.notes: Fault indicator, OPEN-DRAIN, ACTIVE LOW (Table 5-1: 'This pin is an open drain output'; sec 8.3.7). Needs an external pull-up resistor to a logic rail. Asserts on undervoltage, overvoltage, overload, power limiting, ILIM pin short, and thermal shutdown; internally de-glitched. R(FLT) pull-down = 70 ohm typ (36-130 ohm); leakage +/-150 nA. Sink current 10 mA abs max, so size the pull-up accordingly. Rated to 60 V rec / 67 V abs max, so it may be pulled up to a high rail if needed. Leave floating or connect to GND if unused. Assertion delays: 11 us typ after UVLO/OVP trip, 1.3 ms typ during current/power limiting.

pinout.name: PGOOD
pinout.notes: Power Good, OPEN-DRAIN, ACTIVE HIGH (sec 8.3.8: 'open drain Power Good (PGOOD) indicator output'; Table 5-1: 'Active High. A high indicates that the internal FET is enhanced'). Needs an external pull-up - sec 8.3.8: 'PGOOD is rated for 60 V and can be pulled to IN or OUT through a resistor'; sec 9.2.2.3.1 recommends R(PGOOD) = 10 kohm to 100 kohm and the sink current must not exceed 10 mA (abs max). Goes low when the FET turns OFF during a fault or when SHDN is pulled low. Deglitch t(PGOODR) = 11.5 ms typ rising, t(PGOODF) = 10 ms typ falling. R(PGOOD) pull-down 70 ohm typ; leakage +/-150 nA. Can be used to enable/disable downstream DC/DCs. Connect to GND or leave floating if unused.

pinout.name: N.C
pinout.notes: No connect (Table 5-1).

pinout.name: OUT
pinout.notes: Power output (SOURCE of the internal FET). OUT is pins 18, 19 and 20 on HTSSOP - all three must be connected and share the load current (sec 8.3.9: 'Do not leave any of the IN and OUT pins un-connected').

pinout.name: OUT
pinout.notes: Power output, parallel with pins 18 and 20. Must be connected.

pinout.name: OUT
pinout.notes: Power output, parallel with pins 18 and 19. Must be connected.

pinout.name: PowerPAD
pinout.notes: Exposed thermal pad, numbered 21 in the TI land pattern drawing 4224598/A. Table 5-1: 'Connect PowerPAD to GND plane for heat sinking. Do not use PowerPAD as the only electrical connection to GND.' Sec 9.5.1: 'To operate at rated power, the PowerPAD must be soldered directly to the board GND plane directly under the device.'

decoupling.value: 0.1 uF minimum ceramic, IN to GND
decoupling.placement: as close as possible to the IN pins; sec 9.5.1 'TI recommends a 0.1 uF or higher value ceramic decoupling capacitor between IN terminal and GND'
decoupling.notes: Recommended Operating Conditions list 0.1 uF as the MIN external capacitance on IN, P_IN and OUT. Sec 9.2.2.3.1: 'The CIN is a local bypass capacitor to suppress noise at the input. TI recommends a minimum of 0.1 uF for C(IN).' Sec 9.4: if the input supply is more than a few inches away, use an input ceramic bypass capacitor higher than 0.1 uF. Sec 9.4.1: where a TVS is fitted for surge, 'TI recommends to place at least 1 uF of input capacitor'; C(IN) also damps the positive input spike generated by input inductance when the FET interrupts a short, per Vspike(absolute) = V(IN) + I(LOAD) x sqrt(L(IN)/C(IN)) [Eq 14]. P_IN is tied directly to IN and shares this bypass.

decoupling.value: 0.1 uF minimum ceramic, OUT to GND (bulk C(OUT) sized by the load; TI's 1 A example uses 100 uF)
decoupling.notes: Recommended Operating Conditions: external capacitance on IN, P_IN, OUT MIN 0.1 uF. C(OUT) directly sets inrush via I(INRUSH) = C(OUT) x V(IN)/t(dVdT) [Eq 1], so it must be co-designed with C(dVdT). Sec 9.4.1 also recommends a Schottky diode from OUT to GND, placed physically close to the OUT and GND pins, to absorb the negative spike produced by output inductance when the FET interrupts a short.

decoupling.value: C(dVdT) >= 10 nF to GND when slew-rate control is used (leave open for the fast 24 V/500 us ramp with thermal regulation)
decoupling.placement: close to the dVdT pin, with the return leg to GND on the shortest possible trace (sec 9.5.1)
decoupling.notes: Recommended Operating Conditions give 10 nF as the MIN C(dVdT); the timing table specifies UVLO/OVP turn-on delays only for C(dVdT) >= 10 nF. TI's 1 A / 100 uF / 300 mA-inrush example uses 22 nF; Figure 8-1 uses 100 nF with C(OUT) = 1000 uF.

decoupling.value: NO capacitor - do not bypass IMON
decoupling.placement: R(IMON) only, from IMON to GND, close to the pin
decoupling.notes: Sec 8.3.6: 'The IMON pin must not have a bypass capacitor to avoid delay in the current monitoring information.'

land_pattern.package: PWP0020T PowerPAD TSSOP-20, TI land pattern drawing 4224598/A (10/2018)
land_pattern.notes: From the RECOMMENDED 'EXAMPLE BOARD LAYOUT' drawing 4224598/A: 20X (1.5 x 0.45) mm signal pads with (R0.05) corner radius, 18X (0.65) mm pitch, (5.8) mm between the two pad-row centerlines, overall pad-field height (6.5) mm. Pad 21 is the thermal pad and is SOLDER-MASK DEFINED: exposed metal (2.96 x 2.96) mm inside a (3.4 x 6.5) mm copper area covered by solder mask (NOTE 9: 'Size of metal pad may vary due to creepage requirement'). Signal pads: non-solder-mask-defined preferred, 0.05 mm max mask clearance all around (0.05 mm min if solder-mask defined). Stencil (0.125 mm thick): 20X (1.5 x 0.45) apertures plus a (2.96 x 2.96) thermal aperture; alternates 3.31 x 3.31 at 0.1 mm, 2.70 x 2.70 at 0.15 mm, 2.50 x 2.50 at 0.175 mm stencil. Package outline: body 4.3-4.5 mm x 6.4-6.6 mm, lead span 6.2-6.6 mm TYP, lead width 0.19-0.30 mm, 1.2 mm max height, JEDEC MO-153.

exposed_pad.connect_to: GND - 'Connect PowerPAD to GND plane for heat sinking. Do not use PowerPAD as the only electrical connection to GND.' (Table 5-1). Sec 9.5.1: to operate at rated power the PowerPAD must be soldered directly to the board GND plane directly under the device; other planes such as the bottom side can be used to increase heat sinking.

layout_notes: Place a 0.1 uF or higher ceramic decoupling capacitor between the IN terminal and GND (sec 9.5.1).
Keep high-current power-path connections as short as possible and size them to carry at least twice the full-load current (sec 9.5.1).
Locate every support component - R(ILIM), C(dVdT), R(IMON), and the UVLO/OVP divider resistors - close to its own pin, and return the other end to GND with the shortest possible trace (sec 9.5.1).
Route R(ILIM) as short as possible to reduce parasitic effects on current-limit accuracy; these traces must not couple to any switching signal on the board (sec 9.5.2).

Place protection devices (TVS, snubbers, capacitors, diodes) physically close to the device they protect, on short low-inductance traces; in particular the protection Schottky that absorbs negative transients from inductive load switching must be physically close to the OUT and GND pins (sec 9.5.2).

Thermal: solder the PowerPAD directly to the board GND plane directly under the device to reach rated power; use additional planes (e.g. bottom side) for higher-current applications (sec 9.5.2). RthetaJA = 32.2 C/W and RthetaJC(bot) = 3.6 C/W for the 20-pin PWP.

TI's example board layout puts 9 vias of (0.2) mm diameter on a (1.3) mm grid inside the 2.96 x 2.96 mm exposed thermal pad, with a further 6 vias in the mask-covered metal above and below it; vias under paste should be filled, plugged or tented (drawing note 10). Vias are optional depending on application.

Use a large PCB GND plane and minimise lead length/inductance into and out of the device - input inductance produces a positive spike on IN and output inductance a negative spike on OUT when the FET interrupts a short or overload (sec 9.4.1).
The IMON pin must not have a bypass capacitor (sec 8.3.6).
Do not leave any IN or OUT pin unconnected, and connect P_IN directly to IN (sec 8.3.9).
UVLO must not be left floating; tie it to IN if the undervoltage function is unused (sec 8.3.2).

The example 2-layer HTSSOP layout (Figure 9-12) runs a VIN plane into the IN/P_IN side and a VOUT plane out of the OUT side, with top- and bottom-layer GND planes stitched by vias under the PowerPAD and a high-frequency bypass cap adjacent to the IN pins.
